- Question a, wording: The right option claims the images of burnt trees 'alone do not set' a sad mood, and the why repeats this. Bleak images can set a grim mood on their own. rejected.title: Combining modes in multimodal texts
card: A multimodal text uses more than one mode to make meaning. Modes include written and spoken words, images, sound and movement.
Each mode adds something the others cannot. Words can explain, images can show, sound can set a mood and movement can show change over time.
The modes work together. A picture can back up a caption, add to it, or even disagree with it so the viewer notices the gap.
To analyse a multimodal text, ask what each mode adds and how the modes combine to shape the audience's response.
rejected.remember: Each mode adds its own meaning, and the combination shapes the response.

a.q: A short film about a bushfire uses slow, low music over images of burnt trees. What does the music add?
opts: A sad, heavy mood that the images alone do not set
A list of facts about how the fire started
Movement that shows the fire spreading over time
A caption that names the place in the images
a.why: Sound can set a mood, and slow, low music creates a heavy feeling. The images show the burnt trees but do not make the mood by themselves. Music does not give facts or name places.

b.q: A poster for a school recycling drive shows a clean beach. The headline says the beach is already ruined. What effect does this mix of image and words have?
opts: The clash makes viewers stop and think about the claim
The image repeats exactly what the headline says
The headline is made pointless by the image
The poster becomes a text that uses only one mode
b.why: The picture and words disagree, so viewers notice the gap and think about it. Here the modes do not repeat each other. The poster still uses two modes, words and image.
b.clue: Do the image and words say the same thing here?

problems.detail: 'The modes are written words, images, sound and movement' reads as a complete list. The Australian Curriculum's examples of modes also include spoken language, and multimodal theory adds gestural and spatial modes. Wording such as 'Modes include…' would avoid teaching a closed list.

a.q: A short film about a bushfire plays slow, low music over images of burnt trees. What does the music most likely add?
opts: A sad, heavy feel that adds to what we see
Facts that explain how the fire first started
Movement that shows the fire spreading over time
A caption that names the place shown in the images
a.why: Sound can set a mood, and slow, low music gives the scene a sad, heavy feel. The burnt trees may already look grim, and the music deepens that feeling. Music does not explain facts or name places, and it is the images, not the music, that show movement.
a.clue: What does the card say sound can do?

b.q: A recycling drive poster shows a spotless beach, but its headline claims the beach is already ruined. What is the effect of this mix of image and words?
opts: The clash makes viewers stop and think
The image simply repeats what the headline says
The image makes the headline pointless
The poster now works in a single mode
b.why: The picture and the words disagree, so viewers notice the gap and think about why. Here the modes do not repeat each other, and neither cancels the other out. The poster still uses two modes, words and image.
b.clue: Do the image and the headline agree?

a.best: A sad, heavy feel that adds to what we see

b.best: The clash makes viewers stop and think
